source.note: All seven planets between Rahu and Ketu in the natural zodiacal direction. Phase 1.3 splits this into 12 named axis-position variants per Mansagari.
Sun afflicted by Rahu/Ketu/Saturn in 9th house or its lord; ancestral karma carryover.
Saturn in malefic placement (lagna/moon-axis 1/4/7/10) without dignity. Sade Sati overlap is computed separately in `gochar` module.
Jupiter conjunct Rahu (Chandal) or Ketu — wisdom corrupted by shadow planet.
Sun or Moon conjunct Rahu/Ketu in same sign — eclipse imprint at birth. Distinct from `ECLIPSE_DOSHA` (which is birth during an actual eclipse).
No planet (other than Sun and nodes) in 2nd or 12th from Moon, and no planet conjunct Moon — isolation of mind.
Affliction to 5th house lord by Rahu/Ketu, indicating Naga (serpent deity) propitiation pending — primarily affects progeny. Drawn from regional South Indian tradition; no single canonical text.
Severe affliction to Jupiter (combust + debilitated, or in 6/8/12 with malefics) — corrupted dharma karaka. Synthesized from BPHS Ch.7 affliction principles applied to Jupiter as Brahma-karaka.

source.note: Birth in Mool/Jyeshtha/Ashlesha/Magha/Revati nakshatras — the five "mool" (root) nakshatras. Mandatory check in Nepali tradition; severity grades by pada (1st pada most severe; later padas progressively milder per Narada Samhita).

Sun or Moon at sign-junction within 3°20' (200 arc-minutes) of Pisces→Aries, Cancer→Leo, or Scorpio→Sagittarius. The water-fire transitions are doctrinally most severe; affects health and longevity at birth. Detection is longitude-based, not panchanga-tabular.
Birth during Vishti (Bhadra) karana. Vishti is the 7th of the seven movable karanas; presence at birth threatens stability of activities undertaken in early life.

Birth on a sankranti day (the Sun crossing a sign boundary, ±6 hours). Considered inauspicious by Muhurta Ganapati; affects status of the early life. Window configurable via `PanchangaSnapshot.onSankranti`.
Birth on Amavasya (new moon). The Moon is at minimum strength (combust with Sun); affects emotional stability and mother. Distinct from Krishna-Paksha Dosha which fires for any waning-moon birth.

Birth in Krishna Paksha (waning lunar fortnight, post-Purnima through Amavasya). The Moon's natural strength wanes; mild psychological vulnerability. Distinct from Amavasya Dosha (specific to new-moon day) and Vish Yoga (Saturn+Moon affliction).
Birth on Rikta tithis (4th, 9th, 14th of either paksha — Chaturthi, Navami, Chaturdashi). These are doctrinally inauspicious tithis for new beginnings; presence at birth carries a mild affliction.

Specific vara-nakshatra combinations (e.g. Sunday + Magha, Monday + Vishakha, etc.) form Yamaghanta — a "death-bell" yoga inauspicious for any major life beginning. Phase 1.2 currently flags only the nakshatra side; full vara-nakshatra pair table will land in Phase 1.2 addendum.
Birth during Vyatipata yoga (17th of the 27 panchanga yogas). Doctrinally inauspicious for any auspicious activity; presence at birth threatens stability of fortune.
Birth during Vaidhriti yoga (27th and last of the panchanga yogas). Like Vyatipata, doctrinally inauspicious; presence at birth threatens stability of important undertakings.

Birth during a solar or lunar eclipse window — distinct from `GRAHAN_DOSHA` (Sun/Moon conjunct Rahu/Ketu in the natal chart). Eclipse-time birth is doctrinally one of the most inauspicious conditions; severe lifelong remedial work is recommended. Sources: traditional Nepali/Indian astrologer practice; not a single canonical text.

Parashara visha-kanya matrix — a vara + tithi + nakshatra coincidence: Sunday + Dvitiya + Ashlesha, Saturday + Saptami + Krittika, or Tuesday + Dvadashi + Shatabhisha. The tithi rule is by number within the fortnight (both pakshas). Cancellation (Parashara): a benefic in the 7th from Lagna or the 7th-lord in own/exalted sign. A marital-harmony affliction; surfaced for both natal reading and Milan.

Birth in the last pada of Jyeshtha or the first pada of Moola — the exact Jyeshtha-Moola junction at the Scorpio→Sagittarius water-fire boundary. The most severe variant of Gandanta/Mool per Narada (and Vashistha/Brhaspati on the ghatika-extent). Indicates acute early-childhood survival/health sensitivities and a transformational family crisis; mandatory shanti within 27 days.

Jyotirvidyabharanam (carried in Muhurta Chintamani): the birth tithi 'burns' specific signs (e.g. Pratipada → Libra & Capricorn; Shashthi → Aries & Leo). Any of the seven true grahas in a burnt sign has its significations scorched. Detection needs the tithi-to-sign table; owned by the DAGDHA_RASHI custom result hook.

Per Jataka Parijata, each graha has a fatal 'death-portion' degree in each sign; a graha within ~1° of its Mrityu Bhaga turns its significations toward affliction (Mrityu = death-like). Luminaries and the Lagna at Mrityu Bhaga are the classical arishta trigger. Detection is degree-table-based; owned by the MRITYU_BHAGA custom result hook.

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 1. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Anant Kalsarpa Dosha variant is comparatively milder (early-life houses).

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 2. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Kulik Kalsarpa Dosha variant is comparatively milder (early-life houses).

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 3. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Vasuki Kalsarpa Dosha variant is comparatively milder (early-life houses).

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 4. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Shankhpal Kalsarpa Dosha variant has moderate severity per the classical commentary.

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 5. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Padma Kalsarpa Dosha variant has moderate severity per the classical commentary.

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 6. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Mahapadma Kalsarpa Dosha variant has moderate severity per the classical commentary.

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 7. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Takshak Kalsarpa Dosha variant is among the most severe (kendra/mortality axis).

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 8. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Karkotak Kalsarpa Dosha variant is among the most severe (kendra/mortality axis).

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 9. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Shankhachud Kalsarpa Dosha variant has moderate severity per the classical commentary.

Kalsarpa axis-position variant: Rahu in house 10. Each of the 12 Mansagari named variants carries doctrinally distinct effects — Ghatak Kalsarpa Dosha variant has moderate severity per the classical commentary.

Auspicious mirror of Kalsarpa: all seven planets between Ketu and Rahu (the reverse arc). Confers gradual prosperity and protection — classical Mansagari distinguishes this from Kalsarpa, where the same arc-direction ascension is malefic and the descent (Ketu-side dominance) is the auspicious form.

Saturn conjunct Moon — "poison" yoga. Saturnine restriction blocks the Moon's emotional flow; threatens depression, isolation, and chronic mental fatigue. Distinct from `SHANI_DOSHA` (Saturn in house-axis affliction) — Vish requires same-sign Moon-Saturn conjunction. Companion to the yoga-corpus `VISH` rule, which scores strength rather than severity.

Moon afflicted by malefic conjunction (Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu) AND debilitated/in-dusthana. Distinct from Kemdrum (Moon's isolation), distinct from Vish Yoga (specifically Saturn+Moon). General "Moon affliction" diagnosis used by classical practitioners as a category-level flag.

Saturn conjunct Rahu — the "cursed" yoga. Threatens chronic obstacles, ancestral karma carryover, and isolation. Distinct from `PITRA_DOSHA` (Sun-affliction by Rahu/Saturn in 9th-axis) and from `GURU_CHANDAL` (Jupiter+Rahu/Ketu). Severity heightened when in lagna, 5th, or 8th house. Also recognized in traditional Vedic practice; Lal Kitab gives it the most formal treatment.

Mars conjunct Rahu — the "burning coal" yoga (Angarak = "burning coal" in Sanskrit). Threatens accidents, surgeries, sudden anger, and impulsive disputes. The yoga-corpus `MARS_RAHU_CONJ` rule shares this condition and scores strength; `ANGARAK_DOSHA` surfaces the same as a severity-shape dosha. Distinct from `GURU_CHANDAL` (Jupiter+Rahu/Ketu) and `SHRAPIT_DOSHA` (Saturn+Rahu). Drawn from regional traditional usage; not a single canonical text.

Generic Chandal-form yoga: Rahu conjunct any classical planet other than Jupiter (which is the canonical `GURU_CHANDAL` case). When Rahu meets Sun (royal authority), Moon (mind), Mercury (intellect), or Venus (refinement), each carries the Chandal "shadow-pollution" theme. Distinct from named-specific doshas (Angarak=Mars+Rahu, Shrapit=Saturn+Rahu, Guru-Chandal=Jupiter+Rahu/Ketu); this rule covers the remaining Sun/Moon/Mercury/Venus combinations.

Benefic planets owning a kendra (1/4/7/10) lose their natural benefic potency. Detection: any natural benefic (Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, Moon) is the lord of a kendra. Cancellation: the same benefic also rules a trikona (1/5/9) — the trikona ownership preserves benefic effect (Lagna-lord excepted; Lagna IS both kendra and trikona, so 1st-lord benefics carry no Kendradhipati taint). The doctrinal nuance is rich; Phase 1.4 captures the canonical "any benefic owns a pure kendra" trigger.

Severe poverty pattern: Lagna-lord in dusthana (6/8/12) AND 11th-lord in dusthana — combined affliction of self and gain. Distinct from the yoga-corpus `DARIDRA_*` rules which are single-condition strength yogas. The dosha shape surfaces severity (a stronger flag for chart-output prominence) and accumulates remedies.

5th-house affliction indicating progeny challenges: 5th-lord debilitated, in dusthana, OR Jupiter (putra-karaka) afflicted. Distinct from `NAGA_DOSHA` which targets 5th via Rahu/Ketu specifically. Putra Dosha is a broader bhava-affliction reading.

4th-house affliction indicating mother's health/longevity challenges: 4th-lord debilitated/in dusthana, OR Moon (matri-karaka) afflicted. Distinct from Chandra Dosha which evaluates Moon affliction across multiple triggers without 4th-house focus.

7th-house affliction indicating spouse health/marital harmony challenges: 7th-lord debilitated/in dusthana, OR Venus (kalatra-karaka) afflicted. Distinct from MANGAL_DOSHA which is Mars-specific. PATNI_DOSHA is the broader 7th-house bhava-affliction reading from BPHS Ch.30.

Family / relatives affliction synthesis: 4th-lord (immediate family/home) AND 11th-lord (elder siblings/community) both in dusthana. Indicates strain in relationships with relatives, family disputes, or estrangement. Drawn from regional traditional usage as a category-level flag; no single canonical text — uses 4th + 11th double-affliction pattern from BPHS Ch.24 read as a compound dosha.

Lal Kitab Pitri Rina (ancestral karmic debt) surfaced as a dosha. Conditions mirror `LalkitabRinaService.detectAll()` for the pitri rina type: Sun-Rahu conjunction in 2/5/9, Sun in 6/8/12, or Jupiter in 10. Same conditions, different shape — the rina-shape carries Lal Kitab specific affliction trace; the dosha-shape feeds unified chart-output rendering alongside Pitra Dosha (which is BPHS-derived).
Lal Kitab Stri Rina (spousal/female karmic debt) surfaced as a dosha. Conditions mirror the Lal Kitab rina detector for stri rina: Venus-Rahu in 4/7, Moon-Ketu in 2/7, Venus in 1/8.
Lal Kitab Swajan Rina (relative/self karmic debt) surfaced as a dosha. Conditions mirror the Lal Kitab rina detector for swajan rina: Mercury-Ketu in 1/6/8, Saturn in 1/4, Mars-Saturn in 6/8.

BPHS badhaka-sthana: the 11th from a movable Lagna, the 9th from a fixed Lagna, the 7th from a dual Lagna. The dosha fires when a natural malefic occupies the badhaka-sthana or the Badhakesh (its lord) sits in a dusthana (6/8/12). Cancellation: Badhakesh in own/exalted/mooltrikona or in an upachaya (3/6/11). Detection needs the Lagna-modality lookup; owned by the BADHAKA custom result hook.
